properties.NoteContent: CRITICAL: Pure contributory negligence state. If the insured is even 1% at fault, they may be barred from recovery. Investigate all third-party liability meticulously.
HIGH PRIORITY: Extreme weather handling applies. If the vehicle is non-drivable outside of Anchorage or Fairbanks, verify remote towing limits before dispatching recovery services.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Zero deductible glass state if the insured purchased full safety glass coverage. Do not apply the comprehensive deductible for windshield repair or replacement claims.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Modified comparative fault (50% rule). If our driver is 50% or more at fault, they cannot recover from the other party. Gather independent witness statements early.

CRITICAL: Strict adherence to Fair Claims Settlement Practices Regulations. If claimant requests repair guidance, provide the approved repair-choice disclosure and note whether the vehicle is garaged in-state or out-of-state. If injuries are reported, do not speculate on medical payments or liability outcomes.
HIGH PRIORITY: Frequent catastrophic hail claims. Check for Uninsured Motorist Property Damage (UMPD) and verify if winter traction laws apply if the accident occurred in the mountainous zones.

CRITICAL: Strict regulations on aftermarket and salvage parts. Ensure the estimate complies with OEM part guidelines for newer vehicles. Do not mandate non-OEM parts without explicit customer disclosure.

MEDIUM PRIORITY: Mandatory PIP state. If injuries are reported, establish the PIP claim immediately. Do not speculate on medical payments or liability outcomes before the PIP adjuster reviews the file.

name: Handling Note - Personal Auto - District of Columbia

properties.NoteContent: HIGH PRIORITY: Claimants have 60 days to elect whether to receive PIP benefits or pursue a tort claim against the at-fault driver. Note the exact date of loss and transfer to the DC PIP queue.

CRITICAL: 14-Day PIP Rule applies. The insured must seek medical treatment within 14 days of the accident to access their full PIP benefits. Additionally, Florida mandates a zero-deductible for windshield replacements.
CRITICAL: Diminished Value (17c formula) must be assessed on all first-party collision claims. Automatically refer the vehicle to the DV evaluation queue once physical repairs are completed.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: No-fault state with strict injury thresholds. Note whether the vehicle was shipped inter-island and establish the injury claim under Hawaii PIP guidelines.
LOW PRIORITY: Standard comparative negligence. Document road conditions and ensure timely appraisal assignment. No unusual statutory requirements for initial intake.
HIGH PRIORITY: Modified comparative fault (51% rule). Ensure swift evaluation of intersection accidents. For total losses, verify local salvage and title retention rules.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Modified comparative fault (51%). For any claims involving state property or municipal vehicles, a tort claim notice must be filed within 180 days.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Modified comparative fault (51%). Ask the caller specifically about farm equipment or rural road conditions, as these frequently impact liability assessments.
HIGH PRIORITY: No-fault PIP state. Promptly identify any medical providers and explain Kansas PIP benefits. Do not discuss bodily injury settlements until PIP is exhausted.
HIGH PRIORITY: Choice no-fault state. Verify on the dec page if the insured formally rejected PIP (No-Fault) coverage. If PIP is active, route to the KY PIP unit.

CRITICAL: No Pay, No Play statute in effect. If the claimant was uninsured at the time of the accident, they are barred from collecting the first $15,000 of bodily injury and $25,000 of property damage.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Modified comparative fault (50% rule). Verify the presence of animals (e.g., moose collisions) and process under comprehensive coverage rather than collision.
CRITICAL: Pure contributory negligence state. Any negligence by the claimant bars recovery. Obtain recorded statements from all parties immediately.

CRITICAL: Strict no-fault state. Safe Driver Insurance Plan (SDIP) rules apply. Fault determinations must align with MA Division of Insurance Standards of Fault. Advise the customer of the appeals process if they are found at fault.

CRITICAL: Michigan No-Fault rules apply. Determine if the insured has Broad Form Collision, Standard, or Limited. If the other party is at fault, explain the Michigan Mini-Tort recovery process ($3,000 max).
HIGH PRIORITY: No-fault state. High PIP limits apply. For any injuries, immediately assign a MN PIP adjuster and provide the mandatory no-fault packet within 30 days.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Pure comparative fault. Even if our driver is 99% at fault, the claimant can recover 1% of their damages. Thoroughly document all contributing factors.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Pure comparative fault state. Document the scene accurately. There are no restrictive caps on non-economic damages for auto accidents.
HIGH PRIORITY: Modified comparative fault (51%). Inform the insured of their right to use the repair facility of their choice. Anti-steering laws are strictly enforced.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Modified comparative fault (50%). Gather the police report immediately to confirm traffic control devices and right-of-way for intersection claims.
HIGH PRIORITY: Modified comparative fault (51%). Note any involvement of rideshare (Uber/Lyft) or delivery services, as Las Vegas has high TNC frequency. Check the TNC endorsement.

name: Handling Note - Personal Auto - New Hampshire

properties.NoteContent: HIGH PRIORITY: Auto insurance is not strictly mandatory, leading to high UM/UIM exposure. Verify UM/UIM limits immediately if the at-fault party is uninsured.

name: Handling Note - Personal Auto - New Jersey

properties.NoteContent: CRITICAL: Complex No-Fault state. Verify if the policy has the Limitation on Lawsuit (Verbal Threshold) or No Threshold. This dictates their ability to sue for pain and suffering.

name: Handling Note - Personal Auto - New Mexico

properties.NoteContent: MEDIUM PRIORITY: Pure comparative fault. Ensure all involved vehicles and witnesses are contacted to establish exact negligence percentages.

name: Handling Note - Personal Auto - New York

properties.NoteContent: CRITICAL: Regulation 64 compliance is mandatory. Strict timelines for inspections and settlement offers. New York No-Fault (PIP) must be opened for any vehicle occupant injuries. Provide the mandatory NY photo inspection disclosures.

name: Handling Note - Personal Auto - North Carolina

properties.NoteContent: CRITICAL: Pure contributory negligence state. The 1% rule applies. Thoroughly investigate claimant negligence before accepting liability for property damage or bodily injury.

name: Handling Note - Personal Auto - North Dakota

properties.NoteContent: HIGH PRIORITY: No-fault PIP state. Threshold for tort claims is $2,500 in medical expenses or severe injury. Route injury claims directly to ND PIP adjusters.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Modified comparative fault (51%). Ensure swift appraisal assignment. Note whether the vehicle is garaged in-state or out-of-state for rental tax purposes.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Modified comparative fault (51%). Verify tribal land jurisdiction if the accident occurred on a reservation, as this can affect liability and tort laws.
HIGH PRIORITY: PIP is mandatory for all policies. Determine if the claimant is a bicyclist or pedestrian, as OR PIP extends to non-occupants struck by the insured vehicle.
CRITICAL: Choice No-Fault state. Verify if the insured selected Full Tort or Limited Tort. Limited Tort restricts the ability to sue for non-monetary damages unless injuries are "serious."

name: Handling Note - Personal Auto - Rhode Island

properties.NoteContent: MEDIUM PRIORITY: Pure comparative fault. Ensure the insured is aware they can select their own repair shop. Rhode Island heavily regulates the use of aftermarket parts on newer vehicles.

name: Handling Note - Personal Auto - South Carolina

properties.NoteContent: MEDIUM PRIORITY: Modified comparative fault (51%). Punitive damages are common in DUI or reckless driving cases; escalate if a police report notes egregious traffic violations.

name: Handling Note - Personal Auto - South Dakota

properties.NoteContent: HIGH PRIORITY: Follows a unique "Slight/Gross" negligence rule rather than a strict percentage. If the plaintiff's negligence is more than slight, they are barred from recovery.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Modified comparative fault (50%). Verify if the accident involved uninsured motorists, as TN has specific requirements for physical contact in hit-and-run UM claims.

CRITICAL: Modified comparative fault (51%). Verify Named Driver Exclusions carefully. If the driver is excluded on the Texas policy, there is absolutely no coverage. Texas also requires swift resolution under Chapter 542 of the Insurance Code.
HIGH PRIORITY: No-fault PIP state. A $3,000 medical expense threshold must be met to step outside the no-fault system. Route all passenger injuries to UT PIP.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Modified comparative fault (51%). Ensure rapid response for winter weather claims. Review towing limits closely as rural tows can easily exceed standard limits.
CRITICAL: Pure contributory negligence state. Any degree of fault on the claimant bars recovery. Secure recorded statements immediately to lock in the facts of the loss.
HIGH PRIORITY: Pure comparative fault. Washington handles diminished value actively. Assess both vehicles for DV potential if the repairs are significant but the vehicle is not a total loss.

name: Handling Note - Personal Auto - West Virginia

properties.NoteContent: MEDIUM PRIORITY: Modified comparative fault (50%). Note whether the accident involved logging trucks, coal trucks, or mountainous terrain which might require specialized field adjusters.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Modified comparative fault (51%). Check for specific animal collision details, as deer hits are processed under comprehensive coverage. Ensure swift appraisal.

MEDIUM PRIORITY: Modified comparative fault (50%). Check jurisdiction for accidents occurring in Yellowstone or Grand Teton National Parks, as federal tort claims act rules may interplay if government vehicles are involved.
